question: \(y=(3x-1)^2\). What is the derivative at \(x=1\)?
solution: The chain rule requires multiplying the derivative of the square by the derivative \(3\) of the inner function \(3x-1\). Thus \(y'=2(3x-1)\times3\). At \(x=1\), this gives \(y'(1)=2\times2\times3=12\).
